visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour has an enterprise value of €1bn, net debt of €300m, €50m of supply chain finance and a €40m pension deficit. What's the equity value?
questions.explain: €1bn minus €300m of net debt, €50m of supply chain finance and €40m of pension deficit. €700m stops at net debt; €200m treats the €50m as if it were EBITDA.
questions.explain_at: Equity value, six hundred and ten million

questions.q: Under IAS 37, where does a lawsuit appear if the company could possibly lose it, but probably won't?

options.text: In the notes, with no provision
As a provision for the full claim
As a provision for the expected cost

questions.explain: A provision is booked when losing is probable and the cost can be estimated. Possible but not probable means a description in the notes; remote means nothing.
questions.explain_at: If it's possible but not probable, you only describe it in the notes

questions.q: A buyer finds €50m of supply chain finance, and the company trades at 10x EBITDA. How much does that take off the equity value?
questions.explain: It's a debt, owed once, so it comes off once. The multiple applies to profit that recurs, not to a balance owed.
questions.explain_at: You owe fifty once, so it comes off once

questions.q: The target has a known compliance problem nobody can put a number on. What protects the buyer best?
questions.explain: For an all-or-nothing risk, the sellers pay if it happens, with money held back to back the promise. Insurance generally excludes problems already disclosed.
questions.explain_at: warranty and indemnity insurance usually covers what nobody knew about

questions.q: Alfa Laval pays $700m for NAVTOR, which has estimated 2026 revenue of about $194m. What multiple can you work out?
questions.explain: $700m ÷ $194m ≈ 3.6, and $194m is revenue, so it's a multiple of sales. The release gives no EBITDA, so there's no EBITDA multiple.
questions.explain_at: so three point six is a multiple of sales
